title: A Glory Gilds the Sacred Page
description: A Glory Gilds the Sacred Page in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 186 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Light and Glory of the Word”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A glo-ry gilds the sa-cred page, Ma-jes-tic like the sun: It gives a light to ev-ery age; It gives, but bor-rows none.

lines: A glory gilds the sacred page,
It gives a light to every age;
The hand that gave it still supplies
His truths upon the nations rise;
As makes a world of darkness shine
The steps of Him I love,
Till glory break upon my view

licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
